questions.subtopic: Chapter 1: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants (Embryo Sac)
questions.question: A typical mature angiosperm female gametophyte (embryo sac) at the time of fertilization consists of what cellular and nuclear organization?
options: 7-celled and 8-nucleate
8-celled and 8-nucleate
7-celled and 7-nucleate
6-celled and 8-nucleate
questions.explanation: During megagametogenesis, the functional megaspore undergoes three rounds of free nuclear mitotic divisions producing 8 nuclei. Cytokinesis organizes 3 antipodal cells at the chalazal end, 1 egg cell and 2 synergids (egg apparatus) at the micropylar end, and a large central cell containing 2 polar nuclei: 7 cells and 8 nuclei.

questions.subtopic: Chapter 5: Molecular Basis of Inheritance (Hershey-Chase Experiment)
questions.question: In their 1952 bacteriophage experiment proving DNA as the genetic material, Hershey and Chase labeled DNA and protein coats respectively using which radioactive isotopes?

35S for DNA and 32P for protein coat
14C for DNA and 15N for protein coat
3H for DNA and 14C for protein coat

questions.subtopic: Chapter 6: Evolution (Hardy-Weinberg Principle)
questions.question: Which evolutionary factor disrupts the genetic equilibrium of a Mendelian population according to the Hardy-Weinberg law (p² + 2pq + q² = 1)?
options: Gene flow, genetic drift, mutation, genetic recombination, and natural selection
Random mating in an infinitely large population
Absence of differential reproductive mortality
Uniform environmental conditions over geological epochs
questions.explanation: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium holds when allele frequencies remain constant in the absence of evolutionary influences. Five factors disrupt this equilibrium: gene migration (gene flow), genetic drift, mutation, genetic recombination during meiosis, and natural selection.

questions.subtopic: Chapter 10: Biotechnology and Its Applications (Bt Cotton)
questions.question: Why does the crystalline Bt toxin produced by Bacillus thuringiensis kill lepidopteran insect larvae but not harm the host bacterium or mammalian digestive tracts?
options: The inactive protoxin is solubilized and activated only in the alkaline pH of the insect midgut, binding epithelial receptors to form lytic pores
Mammalian stomach acid activates the protoxin into a harmless vitamin
The bacterium contains antitoxin enzymes that hydrolyze all crystal proteins
The crystal protein binds only to plant cellulose microfibrils
questions.explanation: Bt toxin exists as an inactive crystal protoxin in bacteria. Ingested by insect larvae, the alkaline pH (>9.0) of the midgut solubilizes the crystals, and gut proteases cleave the protoxin into active toxin. The active toxin binds midgut epithelial receptors, creating pores that cause cell lysis and death.

questions.subtopic: Chapter 11: Organisms and Populations (Population Growth)
questions.question: In the logistic population growth equation dN/dt = rN[(K - N) / K], what does the term (K - N) / K represent ecologically?
options: Environmental resistance to population growth as carrying capacity K is approached
Intrinsic rate of natural increase under ideal un-limited conditions
Total mortality rate per thousand individuals
Net immigration rate across geographical borders
questions.explanation: In the Verhulst-Pearl logistic equation, (K - N) / K represents environmental resistance (fraction of carrying capacity still available). When N is small, this term is close to 1 (exponential growth); as N approaches K, (K - N) / K approaches 0, slowing growth to an asymptote.

questions.subtopic: Chapter 12: Biodiversity and Conservation (Species-Area Relationship)
questions.question: Alexander von Humboldt observed that within a region, species richness increases with explored area up to a limit. On a logarithmic scale, what is the mathematical equation of this relationship?
options: log S = log C + Z * log A
log S = log C - Z * log A
log S = Z * log C + log A
S = C * A^Z
questions.explanation: The species-area relationship is described by S = C * A^Z, where S is species richness, A is area, C is y-intercept, and Z is the slope of the regression line. On a log-log scale, it yields a straight line: log S = log C + Z * log A (where Z typically ranges between 0.1 and 0.2 for local areas).
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology — Chapter 12: Biodiversity and Conservation, Page 262

questions.subtopic: Chapter 1: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants (Apomixis)
questions.question: What is apomixis in flowering plants, and in which plant families is it commonly observed?
options: Form of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction by producing seeds without fertilization, seen in Asteraceae and Poaceae (grasses)
Development of fruit directly without fertilization resulting in seedless fruits, seen in Musaceae (banana)
Fusion of two male gametes with a single diploid secondary nucleus in the central cell
Formation of vegetative propagules like runners and stolons from stem nodes in aquatic plants
questions.explanation: Apomixis is a specialized form of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction, where seeds are formed without fertilization. It is common in species of Asteraceae and Poaceae (grasses). In many Citrus and mango varieties, maternal nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac start dividing, protrude into the embryo sac, and develop into multiple embryos (polyembryony).
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 1: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants, Section 1.4 Apomixis and Polyembryony

questions.subtopic: Chapter 2: Human Reproduction (Placental Hormones)
questions.question: Which set of hormones is produced in women exclusively during pregnancy by the human placenta?
options: Estrogen, Progesterone, and Luteinizing Hormone (LH)
Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG), Human Placental Lactogen (hPL), and Relaxin
Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH), Prolactin, and Oxytocin
Thyroxine, Cortisol, and Aldosterone
questions.explanation: The placenta acts as an endocrine tissue and produces several hormones: human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), human placental lactogen (hPL), estrogens, and progestogens. In the later phase of pregnancy, a hormone called relaxin is also secreted by the ovary. hCG, hPL, and relaxin are produced in women only during pregnancy.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 2: Human Reproduction, Section 2.4 Pregnancy and Embryonic Development

questions.subtopic: Chapter 3: Reproductive Health (Assisted Reproductive Technologies)
questions.question: In Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART), what is the key difference between ZIFT (Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer) and IUT (Intra Uterine Transfer)?
options: ZIFT transfers the zygote or early embryo up to 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube, while IUT transfers embryos with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus
ZIFT is an in-vivo fertilization technique, while IUT is an in-vitro fertilization technique
ZIFT transfers unfertilized ova into the ampulla, while IUT transfers washed sperm into the uterine cavity
ZIFT is performed laparoscopically without anesthesia, while IUT requires major surgical incision
questions.explanation: In test-tube baby programs (IVF-ET), the zygote or early embryo (with up to 8 blastomeres) is transferred into the fallopian tube (ZIFT – Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer), whereas embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred directly into the uterus (IUT – Intra Uterine Transfer) to complete further development.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 3: Reproductive Health, Section 3.4 Infertility

questions.subtopic: Chapter 4: Principles of Inheritance (Incomplete Dominance)
questions.question: When a true-breeding red-flowered snapdragon (Antirrhinum majus, RR) is crossed with a true-breeding white-flowered plant (rr), the F1 plants have pink flowers (Rr). What phenotypic ratio is obtained in the F2 generation upon selfing F1?
options: 3 Red : 1 White
1 Red : 2 Pink : 1 White
9 Red : 3 Pink : 3 White : 1 Yellow
All Pink flowers
questions.explanation: In Snapdragon (Antirrhinum majus), flower colour exhibits incomplete dominance. Crossing red (RR) with white (rr) yields pink (Rr) F1 hybrids. When F1 is self-pollinated, the F2 generation yields genotypes 1 RR : 2 Rr : 1 rr. Because the heterozygote Rr has a distinct pink phenotype, the phenotypic ratio matches the genotypic ratio: 1 Red (RR) : 2 Pink (Rr) : 1 White (rr).
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 4: Principles of Inheritance and Variation, Section 4.2.2.1 Incomplete Dominance

questions.subtopic: Chapter 4: Principles of Inheritance (Co-dominance & Multiple Alleles)
questions.question: In human ABO blood groups, alleles I^A and I^B are co-dominant, while allele i is recessive. How many different phenotypes and genotypes are possible in the human population for ABO blood grouping?
options: 4 Phenotypes and 6 Genotypes
6 Phenotypes and 4 Genotypes
3 Phenotypes and 6 Genotypes
4 Phenotypes and 4 Genotypes
questions.explanation: ABO blood groups are controlled by the gene I, which has three alleles: I^A, I^B, and i. There are 6 possible genotypes: I^A I^A, I^A i (Blood Group A); I^B I^B, I^B i (Blood Group B); I^A I^B (Blood Group AB); and ii (Blood Group O). These 6 genotypes produce exactly 4 distinct phenotypes (blood groups A, B, AB, and O).
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 4: Principles of Inheritance and Variation, Section 4.2.2.2 Co-dominance

questions.subtopic: Chapter 4: Principles of Inheritance (Sickle-Cell Anemia Point Mutation)
questions.question: Sickle-cell anemia is caused by a point mutation in the beta-globin chain gene of hemoglobin. What exact nucleotide and amino acid substitution occurs?
options: Adenine is replaced by Uracil (GAG to GUG), replacing Glutamic acid by Valine at position 6
Guanine is replaced by Cytosine (GAG to GCG), replacing Glutamic acid by Alanine at position 6
Thymine is replaced by Cytosine (GAT to GAC), replacing Aspartic acid by Asparagine at position 4
Adenine is replaced by Cytosine (GAG to GCG), replacing Lysine by Leucine at position 7
questions.explanation: Sickle-cell anemia results from a single base substitution at the sixth codon of the beta-globin gene from GAG to GUG. In mRNA, the mutant codon GUG translates into valine instead of glutamic acid at the sixth position of the beta-globin polypeptide. The mutant HbS polymerizes under low oxygen tension, causing RBCs to deform into a rigid sickle shape.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 4: Principles of Inheritance and Variation, Section 4.4.2 Mendelian Disorders

questions.subtopic: Chapter 5: Molecular Basis of Inheritance (DNA Structure & Meselson-Stahl)
questions.question: In the Meselson and Stahl experiment demonstrating the semi-conservative replication of DNA, which technique and chemical gradient were used to separate heavy (15N) DNA from light (14N) DNA?
options: Agarose gel electrophoresis with ethidium bromide
Cesium chloride (CsCl) density gradient equilibrium centrifugation
Paper chromatography with an organic solvent system
Sanger chain-termination capillary electrophoresis
questions.explanation: Matthew Meselson and Franklin Stahl (1958) grew E. coli in a medium containing 15NH4Cl (15N is a heavy isotope, not radioactive). They separated 15N-containing DNA from normal 14N-DNA using equilibrium density gradient centrifugation in a cesium chloride (CsCl) solution, proving that each newly synthesized DNA molecule contains one parental and one newly synthesized strand.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 5: Molecular Basis of Inheritance, Section 5.4.2 The Experimental Proof

questions.subtopic: Chapter 5: Molecular Basis of Inheritance (Genetic Code Properties)
questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT a characteristic property of the standard universal genetic code?
options: The code is degenerate because most amino acids are specified by more than one codon
The codon is read on mRNA in a contiguous fashion without punctuations
The codon UAA, UAG, and UGA act as initiator codons that recruit formylmethionine
The genetic code is nearly universal, meaning UUU codes for phenylalanine from bacteria to humans
questions.explanation: UAA (ochre), UAG (amber), and UGA (opal) are stop (nonsense) codons that do not specify any amino acid and signal the termination of polypeptide synthesis. The universal initiator codon is AUG, which codes for Methionine (Met) and serves as the start signal on mRNA.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 5: Molecular Basis of Inheritance, Section 5.5 Genetic Code

questions.subtopic: Chapter 6: Evolution (Homologous vs Analogous Organs)
questions.question: The thorn of Bougainvillea and the tendril of Cucurbita are examples of homologous structures because they:
options: Arise from modified axillary buds and share common anatomical origin, representing divergent evolution
Perform the exact same physiological function of water storage, representing convergent evolution
Originate from different germ layers and represent parallel evolutionary adaptation
Are vestigial organs that have lost ancestral functionality over evolutionary time
questions.explanation: Homologous organs share a common anatomical origin and basic structural plan but perform different functions in response to different adaptations (divergent evolution). Both the thorns of Bougainvillea and tendrils of Cucurbita develop from axillary buds; thorns provide mechanical defense while tendrils provide climbing support.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 6: Evolution, Section 6.3 What are the Evidences for Evolution?

questions.subtopic: Chapter 7: Human Health and Disease (Innate Immunity Barriers)
questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs an innate immunity barrier with its biological example in the human body?
options: Physiological barrier — Lysozyme in tears and saliva, and HCl in gastric juice
Physical barrier — Polymorphonuclear leukocytes (PMNL) and monocytes
Cytokine barrier — Epithelial mucus coating of the respiratory tract
Cellular barrier — Virus-infected cells secreting interferons
questions.explanation: Innate immunity comprises 4 types of barriers: (1) Physical: skin and mucosal lining; (2) Physiological: acid in stomach, saliva in mouth, tears from eyes containing lysozyme; (3) Cellular: phagocytes like PMNL-neutrophils, monocytes, and natural killer (NK) cells; (4) Cytokine: interferons secreted by virus-infected cells to protect non-infected cells.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 7: Human Health and Disease, Section 7.2.1 Innate Immunity

questions.subtopic: Chapter 7: Human Health and Disease (HIV Replication Cycle)
questions.question: Inside the human body, the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) progressively destroys the immune system by selectively attacking and replicating within which specific host cells?
options: B-lymphocytes, preventing humoral antibody secretion
T-helper (CD4+) lymphocytes and macrophages, causing a drastic decline in helper T-cell counts
Erythrocytes, causing severe hemolytic anemia and splenic congestion
Mast cells, causing systemic anaphylaxis and chronic histamine degranulation
questions.explanation: After entering the human body, HIV enters macrophages (which act as an HIV factory) where its RNA genome is reverse-transcribed into viral DNA. Concurrently, HIV attacks CD4+ T-helper lymphocytes, replicates, and releases progeny viruses that attack other helper T-cells, causing a progressive and fatal reduction in T-helper cell count.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 7: Human Health and Disease, Section 7.4 AIDS

questions.subtopic: Chapter 8: Microbes in Human Welfare (Sewage Treatment)
questions.question: In the secondary (biological) treatment of domestic sewage, what occurs during the aeration tank phase?
options: Physical removal of large floating debris through sequential mesh filtration
Vigorous mechanical agitation allows aerobic microbes to form flocs, significantly reducing the Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD)
Methanogenic anaerobic bacteria digest organic sludge to produce biogas (methane, CO2, and H2S)
Chemical precipitation of phosphates using alum and chlorine gas chlorination
questions.explanation: During secondary treatment, primary effluent is passed into large aeration tanks where it is constantly agitated mechanically and air is pumped into it. This allows vigorous growth of useful aerobic microbes into flocs (masses of bacteria associated with fungal filaments). While growing, these microbes consume the major part of organic matter in the effluent, significantly reducing its BOD.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 8: Microbes in Human Welfare, Section 8.2 Microbes in Sewage Treatment

questions.subtopic: Chapter 8: Microbes in Human Welfare (Cyclosporin A & Statins)
questions.question: The immunosuppressive drug Cyclosporin A, widely administered to organ transplant patients to prevent graft rejection, is extracted from which microbial fungus?
options: Trichoderma polysporum
Aspergillus niger
Clostridium butylicum
Saccharomyces cerevisiae
questions.explanation: Cyclosporin A, an invaluable immunosuppressive agent in organ-transplant patients, is produced by the fungus Trichoderma polysporum. In comparison, statins (cholesterol-lowering agents) are produced by the yeast Monascus purpureus.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 8: Microbes in Human Welfare, Section 8.1.3 Chemicals, Enzymes and other Bioactive Molecules

questions.subtopic: Chapter 9: Biotechnology: Principles (pBR322 Cloning Vector Features)
questions.question: In the standard artificial cloning vector plasmid pBR322, what occurs if a foreign gene of interest is ligated into the BamHI restriction recognition site?
options: The origin of replication (ori) is disrupted, terminating plasmid replication
The ampicillin-resistance gene (ampR) undergoes insertional inactivation
The tetracycline-resistance gene (tetR) undergoes insertional inactivation, allowing recombinant selection
The rop gene is duplicated, multiplying the plasmid copy number tenfold
questions.explanation: Plasmid pBR322 contains two antibiotic-resistance marker genes: ampR and tetR. The BamHI site lies within the coding sequence of the tetR gene. Ligation of a foreign DNA fragment at the BamHI site causes insertional inactivation of the tetR gene. Recombinant transformants lose resistance to tetracycline but remain resistant to ampicillin, enabling replica-plating selection.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 9: Biotechnology: Principles and Processes, Section 9.2.2 Cloning Vectors

questions.subtopic: Chapter 9: Biotechnology: Principles (Gel Electrophoresis DNA Staining)
questions.question: Following agarose gel electrophoresis, how are DNA fragments visualized under laboratory conditions?
options: Staining with methylene blue and viewing under visible incandescent white light
Staining with ethidium bromide (EtBr) followed by illumination with ultraviolet (UV) radiation
Autoradiography using radioactive 32P isotopes without any optical lighting
Treating with silver nitrate and examining under a phase-contrast light microscope
questions.explanation: DNA fragments separated on an agarose gel cannot be seen directly in visible light without staining. The gel is stained with ethidium bromide (an intercalating fluorophore) and then exposed to ultraviolet (UV) radiation. DNA fragments appear as bright orange-coloured fluorescent bands.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 9: Biotechnology: Principles and Processes, Section 9.2.1 Separation and Isolation of DNA Fragments

questions.subtopic: Chapter 10: Biotechnology and its Applications (RNA Interference in Tobacco)
questions.question: In RNA interference (RNAi) developed to prevent nematode Meloidogyne incognita infestation in tobacco roots, what vector was used to introduce nematode-specific genes producing both sense and antisense RNA?
options: Bacteriophage lambda
Agrobacterium tumefaciens Ti-plasmid vector
SV40 mammalian viral vector
Bacillus thuringiensis crystal plasmid
questions.explanation: Using Agrobacterium tumefaciens vectors, nematode-specific genes were introduced into the host tobacco plant. The introduction was engineered such that it produced both sense and anti-sense RNA in the host cells. These two complementary RNAs formed a double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) that initiated RNA interference (RNAi) and silenced the specific mRNA of the nematode, preventing its survival.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 10: Biotechnology and its Applications, Section 10.1 Biotechnological Applications in Agriculture

questions.subtopic: Chapter 10: Biotechnology and its Applications (Genetically Engineered Insulin)
questions.question: How did the American company Eli Lilly produce mature human insulin in 1983 using recombinant DNA technology?
options: By synthesizing separate DNA sequences for insulin chains A and B in E. coli and combining them by creating disulfide bonds
By extracting proinsulin from transgenic cow milk and cleaving C-peptide with synthetic trypsin
By culturing human pancreatic beta cells in continuous stirred-tank bioreactors
By cloning the whole human proinsulin gene with C-peptide into Baker's yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae
questions.explanation: In 1983, Eli Lilly prepared two DNA sequences corresponding to chain A and chain B of human insulin and introduced them into plasmids of E. coli to produce chains A and B separately. The extracted chains A and B were then purified and combined by creating disulfide bonds to form active, mature human insulin without the C-peptide.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 10: Biotechnology and its Applications, Section 10.2.1 Genetically Engineered Insulin

questions.subtopic: Chapter 11: Organisms and Populations (Interspecific Population Interactions)
questions.question: An orchid growing as an epiphyte on the branch of a mango tree, and barnacles growing on the back of a whale, are prime ecological examples of which population interaction?
options: Mutualism (+, +)
Commensalism (+, 0)
Amensalism (-, 0)
Parasitism (+, -)
questions.explanation: Commensalism is an interaction between two species where one species derives benefit while the other is neither harmed nor benefited (+, 0). The epiphyte orchid gets physical support and sunlight without deriving nutrition from the mango tree, and the barnacle gets transport and food supply from ocean currents without harming the whale.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 11: Organisms and Populations, Section 11.2 Population Interactions

questions.subtopic: Chapter 12: Ecosystem (Pyramids of Energy & Biomass)
questions.question: Why is an ecological Pyramid of Energy strictly and invariably upright in all ecosystems, without any exceptions?
options: Because primary producers always have a larger physical body size than apex carnivores
Because energy transfer between successive trophic levels obeys the second law of thermodynamics, where approximately 90% is dissipated as heat
Because decomposers actively recycle radiant heat back to autotrophic producers
Because aquatic plankton communities reproduce faster than terrestrial forest trees
questions.explanation: The pyramid of energy is always upright and can never be inverted. When energy flows from a particular trophic level to the next higher level, some energy is always lost as heat in metabolic processes at each step (Lindeman's 10% rule). Hence, the energy available at a higher trophic level is always less than that at lower levels.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 12: Ecosystem, Section 12.5 Ecological Pyramids

questions.subtopic: Chapter 13: Biodiversity and Conservation (In-Situ vs Ex-Situ Conservation)
questions.question: Which of the following conservation strategies is categorized as an EX-SITU (off-site) biodiversity conservation measure?
options: National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries
Biosphere Reserves (e.g., Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve)
Sacred Groves (e.g., Khasi and Jaintia Hills in Meghalaya)
Zoological Parks, Botanical Gardens, and Cryopreservation of gametes
questions.explanation: In ex-situ conservation, threatened animals and plants are taken out from their natural habitat and placed in special settings where they can be protected and given special care: zoological parks, botanical gardens, wildlife safari parks, seed banks, and cryopreservation of gametes. National parks, sanctuaries, biosphere reserves, and sacred groves are in-situ conservation.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 13: Biodiversity and Conservation, Section 13.2.2 How do we Conserve Biodiversity?
